sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification of \(\Delta(\tau)\) is taken as given, and the contribution is uniform row-wise limit and inference theory.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with a fixed finite reported quantile set \(\mathcal T\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with arms classified as Hall-heavy or finite-inverse-moment. Uniform assertions are restricted to laws separated from the phase boundary \(\gamma=2\) and to the learner schedules stated in the armwise theorems.
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity holds almost surely. Heavy arms have a common uniform second-order Hall lower-tail expansion. Finite-inverse-moment arms with finite \(\gamma_a\) inherit a uniform Lindeberg bound from the Hall tail and gamma separation, while \(\gamma_a=\infty\) arms have a common propensity lower bound from the fixed Hölder ball.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each fold uses the constrained boundary-adapted Bernoulli series likelihood. The schedules retain \(J_N\log N/N\to0\) and \(J_N^{-s}\log(N/J_N)\to0\) at \(N=n\) and every refit size \(N=m\). Generalized-inverse scales, order-statistic clips, Hill classification, preliminary quantiles, endpoint scores, drift corrections, and densities are recomputed within each relevant sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 combines Proposition 8.2's deterministic quadratic Knight-remainder and process limit with Proposition 8.3's finite-dimensional infinitely divisible Lévy score limit for the observed true-propensity clipped fixed-quantile estimator.
A growing series-logit propensity fit yields efficient regular-overlap IPW mean estimation.
A nonparametric estimated-propensity QTE estimator is root-\(n\) normal and efficient under regular overlap.
Adaptive scalar \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) resampling yields inference for mean-type effects under irregular identification.
Thresholded cross-fitted AIPW means admit Gaussian inference under tail-amplified nuisance conditions.
Balance-fitted propensities yield regular limit theory for distributional and quantile treatment effects.

body.tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood preserves the compensated infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law uniformly over gamma-separated scheduled rows, while the finite-variance branch admits a uniform learned-propensity Gaussian approximation. The constrained signed Riesz expansion yields the rate \(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\) and the corrected transfer condition \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\). The formally defined moving row variable \(Z_{P,n}=\ell_{1,P,n}L_{1,P}-\ell_{0,P,n}L_{0,P}\) combines the arm laws without requiring convergence of the recombination weights, and fully refitted arm-vector subsampling estimates its law uniformly. The separate critical fold-labelled Poisson question is outside these results.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity. Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results do not provide the singular Hall-boundary signed-functional expansion, a row-wise uniform learned-propensity limit away from \(\gamma=2\), or inference that remains valid under local \(1/\log n\) changes in the two arm scales.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE procedure must preserve signed cancellation at a Hall boundary, use a positive-weight convex argmin and empirical clipping correction, retain the learned-score covariance in regular arms, and approximate the moving two-arm row law rather than force a common fixed limit.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the constrained-sieve log and signed-functional rates, proves the amplified oracle-transfer condition, establishes heavy and Gaussian arm expansions uniformly on their explicit gamma-separated scheduled domains, recombines them into the declared variable \(Z_{P,n}\), and proves uniform conditional validity and pointwise coverage for fully refitted arm-vector subsampling under moving-law anti-concentration.

body.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile benchmark but no feasible propensity-estimation theorem. The present class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) is not literally their published class: it is narrower through its smooth one-dimensional boundary chart and uniform second-order Hall structure, but weaker, and therefore incomparable overall, in requiring only convergence of the finite nested quantile-score vector rather than a full conditional endpoint outcome law. The finite-\(\mathcal T\) oracle law is rederived using score-law factorization, not inherited through class inclusion. Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) motivate regular growing-likelihood projection; the proof here adds singular boundary information geometry and a uniform signed Riesz expansion. Firpo (2007) supplies regular QTE context, while the Gaussian branch here permits finite inverse moments and retains shared first-stage covariance. Heiler and Kazak (2021) motivate irregular subsampling, whereas the proved procedure refits both arm estimators and uses full-sample arm weights to recover the moving row law.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theory excludes a neighborhood of \(\gamma_a=2\), uses a fixed finite quantile set, and is proved on the boundary-smooth class rather than the unrestricted Hall class. That class is narrower than the oracle anchor in chart smoothness and uniform second-order tails but incomparable in endpoint outcomes because only the finite score-vector law is controlled. The approximation-tail conditions are imposed at both full and refitted sample sizes. Coverage is pointwise in each reported quantile, with uniform convergence of finitely many coordinatewise errors, not simultaneous-band coverage. Anti-concentration is assumed directly for the moving row-law family. The critical fold-labelled point-process law is not asserted here.
body.honest_scope: The contribution is feasible uniform row-wise transfer and inference on the explicitly gamma-separated scheduled domain: the constrained likelihood has the displayed signed-functional rate and corrected amplified condition; the positive-weight estimator has a compensated heavy-arm law; the finite-variance estimator has the learned-propensity influence function and a Hall-derived uniform Lindeberg bound; and the normalized QTE is uniformly bounded-Lipschitz close to \(\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\). Fully refitted arm-vector subsampling consistently estimates the same moving law and gives uniform pointwise coverage under the exact moving-law anti-concentration assumption. The \(1/\log n\) example refutes only approximation by fixed limiting mixtures and explains failure of raw scalar subsampling; it does not refute the arm-vector procedure. No claim is made at \(\gamma=2\), for an infinite quantile process, or for the separate critical fold-law question.
body.interpretation: For a varying law \(P\), the inferential object is the moving variable \(Z_{P,n}\), not a single universal weak limit. Fixed unequal heavy-tail indices produce asymptotic dominance by the smaller index, whereas gaps of order \(1/\log n\) keep both arms visible with row-dependent weights. Arm-vector refitting estimates the arm fluctuations at their own subsample scales and restores the full-sample weights, exactly reproducing the row-specific mixture.
